title: POC scoping - Private Networking & Data Residency - Suncrest Health
summary: Initial POC scoping focused on private networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), regional data residency, egress constraints, and benchmark success criteria. Team agreed on a 4-week POC: network setup week, baseline benchmarks, optimized runs, and a validation week. Success criteria: defined SLOs for latency (p50/p95), throughput targets, and audit/compliance evidence (KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO references). Action items captured for both infra and security to validate connectivity and cost estimates.
topics: Benchmarking plan: QPS, token lengths, latency SLOs
Security controls: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML
transcript: 00:00 Jamie Lopez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Jamie, AE at Redwood, and with me is Samir and Olivia on the SE side. 00:12 Nina Alvarez: Hi, Nina here from Suncrest, Ethan, Priya and Laura are on as well. 00:20 Samir Patel: Awesome. high level today is private networking and data residency for the POC, right? 00:28 Ethan Morris: yep, we're primarily concerned about data never leaving our VPC in the US and we have a europe arm that needs eu residency too. 00:36 Priya Shah: and security wants to validate that keys stay in our KMS and audit logs are available, we also need SOC2 alignment. 00:45 Jamie Lopez: understood. quick Q — do you prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink? we can support either for Redwood Private. 00:55 Dr. Laura Kim: From ML perspective latency is big; peering looked simpler but there was talk about cross-account exposures with peering. 01:05 Olivia Chen: right, peering gives lower latency but you have to manage route tables and security groups, whereas PrivateLink gives an interface endpoint and reduces route surface but adds a small hop and potential egress cost. 01:20 Ethan Morris: can you quantify that small hop? like p50 differences we'd expect on meaty requests — 512 token-ish? 01:30 Samir Patel: ballpark — PrivateLink might add 10-30ms depending on region and setup, peering is lower but depends on AZ alignment. for 512 tokens, if using optimized runtime we often see p50 in the 120-200ms range on dedicated hardware; with PrivateLink add ~20ms. 01:50 Nina Alvarez: okay that's helpful. our success criteria will need a p50 under 200ms and p95 under 700ms for standard assistant queries, and throughput of ~50 req/s steady-state. 02:04 Jamie Lopez: good to capture. also important: what network egress constraints? are you blocking public internet entirely? 02:12 Priya Shah: yes, prod VPC has strict egress, outbound only through NAT with proxy and strict firewall rules. we prefer PrivateLink since it avoids NAT traversal but peering is doable if we set up route controls. 02:28 Samir Patel: noted. we'll add both patterns to the POC plan. for PrivateLink we'll provide a service endpoint in your account, you attach an ENI and then traffic stays within AWS fabric — reduced egress. 02:40 Ethan Morris: what about cross-region residency? we have PHI that must stay in us-east-1 for US patients and eu-west-1 for EU. 02:49 Olivia Chen: we can pin model endpoints to region-specific clusters. Redwood Private can be deployed in multiple regions and pinned so data and compute remain in-region. for the POC we'll set up a us-east-1 instance and eu-west-1 read-only setup to validate replication policies. 03:05 Priya Shah: audits — can you push audit logs to our cloudwatch or S3? we need immutable logs for compliance. 03:12 Samir Patel: yes we support pushing audit events to your account; we can also integrate with your KMS for envelope encryption. 03:21 Nina Alvarez: KMS integration is a must. also do you support HSM for key custody? 03:27 Jamie Lopez: we integrate with customer KMS, HSM support via AWS CloudHSM can be arranged for Private deployments — we'll surface architecture doc. 03:35 Dr. Laura Kim: on workload sizing — current traffic estimate is 8M tokens/day with bursty daytime traffic about 75 QPS peak. we want cost estimates for batch vs streaming. 03:47 Olivia Chen: perfect, for sizing we'll ask for typical prompt+response lengths. you said avg 375 tokens per interaction? 03:53 Dr. Laura Kim: yes median is around 300-450 tokens, some long cases up to 1k. 03:59 Samir Patel: for 75 QPS with average 400 tokens and our batching optimizations, a dedicated 4-GPU pool (A10G/RTX-class) might be a starting point but we'll run benchmarks. for a POC we usually allocate 1-2 nodes and synthetic load to validate. 04:15 Ethan Morris: what's the benchmarking plan? we need reproducible numbers and scripts we can run in our env. 04:21 Jamie Lopez: we'll share a benchmark harness (load scripts + dataset) — step one baseline cold-run, step two enable KV/prefix cache, step three quantized model run. we'll capture p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens. 04:36 Priya Shah: can we run a security scan during the POC? vulnerability scan on container images and network config? 04:42 Samir Patel: yes; we'll coordinate image hashes and provide SBOM for the runtime, and SE team can join your security scan window. 04:52 Nina Alvarez: timeline thoughts? 04:55 Jamie Lopez: propose 4 weeks: week 0 (network & account setup), week 1 baseline benchmarks, week 2 optimizations and model tuning, week 3 validation and handoff. 05:07 Ethan Morris: week 0 for peering will need routes and security group changes — we need at least 3 business days for change windows. 05:13 Priya Shah: and a security review at the end of week 2. 05:17 Jamie Lopez: noted; we'll build the schedule with those constraints. 05:22 Dr. Laura Kim: what are your requirements on sample data — do we need to provide de-identified PHI or can we use synthetic? 05:29 Olivia Chen: synthetic is fine for initial perf; if you want end-to-end validation with PHI we recommend encrypted ingestion and explicit approvals — we'll sign DPA and BAA terms before that. 05:42 Nina Alvarez: we have an internal procurement/legal checklist, we'll need your SOC2 attestation and data processing addendum before any PHI is shared. 05:50 Jamie Lopez: we'll share SOC2 report and DPA; legal can coordinate. 05:55 Ethan Morris: costs — I want a rough egress cost estimate if we go peering vs PrivateLink vs NAT egress. 06:03 Samir Patel: peering avoids NAT egress costs but you still pay for cross-AZ or cross-region data transfer. PrivateLink may incur interface endpoint charges plus some data processing fees, but often reduces public egress. we'll provide a cost comparison table. 06:20 Priya Shah: DNS — split-horizon or route 53 private hosted zone? we need internal names to resolve Redwood endpoints. 06:27 Olivia Chen: we usually recommend private hosted zone + endpoint-specific records; we'll include DNS guidance. 06:33 Nina Alvarez: who runs the benchmarking? Redwood or Suncrest? 06:37 Jamie Lopez: collaborative — Redwood will run baseline harness against your endpoint and provide scripts so you can reproduce locally. 06:44 Dr. Laura Kim: can we measure model regression/quality during optimization? we need to ensure quantization doesn't hit clinical accuracy. 06:52 Samir Patel: absolutely — run eval suites and quality metrics. we'll store diffs and rollback to higher precision if quality degrades. 07:00 Ethan Morris: any compliance showstoppers for a PrivateLink-only approach? 07:04 Priya Shah: none immediately, but we'll need to validate that interface endpoints don't leak metadata and that audit logs capture e.g. source IPs. 07:13 Jamie Lopez: we'll provide an architecture doc and sample CloudTrail/CW logs configuration to demonstrate provenance. 07:21 Nina Alvarez: ok next steps and acceptance criteria that we'll sign off on? 07:27 Jamie Lopez: propose acceptance criteria: 1) p50 <200ms and p95 <700ms on 400-token median, 2) throughput >=50 req/s sustained for 10 minutes, 3) KMS and audit log integration validated, 4) SOC2/DPA on file, 5) successful run of security scan with no critical findings. 07:52 Dr. Laura Kim: agree, but add quality gate: no >2% drop in top-n accuracy on clinical prompts when using quantized models. 07:58 Jamie Lopez: got it — add quality gate. 08:02 Ethan Morris: action items and owners? 08:06 Jamie Lopez: we'll recap in notes but high level — Redwood to share network runbook, benchmark harness, SOC2/DPA, cost comparison. Suncrest to open change windows, provide sample prompts/datasets (synthetic or de-id), and run security scan. 08:20 Priya Shah: I'll coordinate security scan window, target two weeks from now. 08:24 Nina Alvarez: procurement will start DPA review today. 08:28 Jamie Lopez: great. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for week 0 kick-off. 08:33 Olivia Chen: any other questions? 08:35 Ethan Morris: none from infra, thanks. 08:37 Dr. Laura Kim: sounds good. 08:40 Jamie Lopez: thanks everyone, we'll send notes and next steps. 08:44 [call ends]
